title: Scalar square for finite exceptional comparison data
statement:
theorem finite_exceptional_formula_scalar
    (BX : Duality D l hl Ω X) (BY : Duality D l hl Ω Y)
    (c : Compactification f)
    (S : ConstructibleExceptionalCoefficients.System l (AuxiliaryClosure.{u} l) D hl (f := f))
    (t : FiniteExceptionalFormulaCore D l hl Ω X f BX BY c S)
    (ht : ∀ E : Index l Ω,
      RationalOperations.DualFormulaAdjunctionNormalized D l hl X c (fieldStage l Ω E)
        (BX.finite.omega E) (BY.finite.omega E) (BX.finite.datum E) (BY.finite.datum E)
        (t.finite E).adjunction) :
    ∀ (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L) (M : Stage l Ω Y E),
      (inclusion L).map ((finiteRightScalar D l hl Ω X f c S E L h).hom.app M) ≫
        (t.comparison L).hom.app ((transition l Ω Y E L h).obj M) =
      (inclusionTransition l Ω X E L h).hom.app
          ((finiteRight D l hl Ω X f c S E).obj M) ≫
        (t.comparison E).hom.app M ≫
        (specifiedExceptionalFormulaCore D l hl Ω X f BX BY).map
          ((inclusionTransition l Ω Y E L h).inv.app M)

source.place: Retained thm-coef-qbar-verdier proof step 9, decomposition introduced by U4

proof.text: For the supplied trace-normalized adjunctions, apply rationalDualFormulaScalarCounit. Transport the system scalar counit identity along rationalLeft. Transpose under the target normalized adjunction; the source and target comparison counit equations, together with naturality of the compact-support scalar comparison, show that scalar extension of the finite exceptional comparison followed by dualScalar equals finiteRightScalar followed by the target comparison.

Expand t.normalized at E and L. Map the finite identity through inclusion_L and apply dual_formula_inclusion_scalar to the remaining duality-pullback-duality components. Naturality of inclusionTransition_X at the finite comparison supplies the final square.

The caller constructs this normalization from the one-field adjunction theorem, so no hypothesis is added to the parent or any target.
